Dotfile is building the AI-native Compliance Operating System for financial institutions. Our mission is to make compliance simple, safe and smart, helping financial institutions onboard customers, manage risk and operate globally.

 

Compliance remains one of the most manual functions in financial services. While most institutions still rely on fragmented tools and human-driven workflows, we believe AI is enabling a fundamental shift toward autonomous compliance. Our ambition is to build Level 5 Compliance: software that can gather evidence, investigate complex situations, assess risk and execute defensible decisions under defined policies.

 

Dotfile has grown into one of Europe’s fastest-growing compliance technology companies. Today, 100+ financial institutions across 15 countries rely on Dotfile for critical compliance operations, with a rapidly growing presence in the US.

 

We recently raised our Series A from leading US and European investors and software operators. We’re now entering our next chapter: investing heavily in product and AI, expanding internationally, and building the team that can make Dotfile the global standard for compliance infrastructure.

 

Role Overview

We are looking for a highly technical, hands-on Product Director to help define and build the next generation of Dotfile.

You will work at the intersection of Product, Engineering, Design and our customers to turn complex compliance problems into simple, powerful product experiences. You will own major areas of the product end-to-end: understanding the problem, designing the system, prototyping solutions, shipping with Engineering, and learning from how customers use them.

This is a builder role. You will be expected to go deep into workflows, data models and technical constraints, work directly with engineers and designers, and prototype ideas yourself when that is the fastest way to move forward. You should care as much about how the underlying system works as you do about the user experience built on top of it.

AI is at the core of Dotfile’s product. You will design systems where agents investigate, reason and act across complex compliance workflows, and use AI extensively in your own work to research, prototype and ship faster.

You will lead a small Product team while remaining deeply involved in the work yourself. You will coach and develop the people on your team, raise the bar for product thinking and execution, and create the environment for them to do their best work. This is not a role where management means stepping away from the product.

You will work directly with the CEO and CTO.

 

Key Responsibilities

  • Own major product areas end-to-end, from understanding the problem and defining the underlying system to shipping, adoption and iteration

  • Lead and develop a small Product team, setting a high bar for product thinking, execution and ownership while remaining deeply hands-on yourself

  • Turn complex compliance workflows into simple, programmable product experiences that can scale across customers, use cases and jurisdictions

  • Work closely with Engineering and Design on product architecture, data models, workflows and technical trade-offs

  • Design how AI agents interact with data, users and other systems to investigate cases, make recommendations and increasingly automate compliance work

  • Prototype ideas quickly using AI and modern development tools to explore interactions, validate concepts and communicate what should be built

  • Spend significant time with customers and internal teams to understand how compliance actually gets done, identify recurring problems and turn them into scalable product capabilities

  • Define clear measures of product success, use data and customer behavior to evaluate what we ship, and iterate quickly when something is not working

  • Continuously improve how we build product at Dotfile, using AI to accelerate research, analysis, prototyping, specification and execution

 

About you

  • You have 6+ years of experience building software products, including significant ownership of complex B2B or infrastructure products

  • You have experience managing and developing product people, while remaining close to the product and comfortable owning problems directly yourself

  • You are deeply technical for a product leader. You are comfortable discussing APIs, data models, system architecture, integrations and technical trade-offs directly with engineers

  • You think in systems. You naturally look beyond individual features to understand the underlying primitives, abstractions and interactions that make a product scalable

  • You are extremely hands-on. You like getting into the details, exploring data, prototyping ideas and working directly with engineers and designers

  • AI is already deeply embedded in how you work. You use LLMs, coding tools and agents to research, analyze, prototype and build, and actively experiment with new capabilities as they emerge

  • You have strong product judgment and can turn ambiguous, complex problems into products that feel simple to users

  • You are comfortable building AI products where outputs are probabilistic and care deeply about evaluation, reliability, observability, human oversight and feedback loops

  • You thrive in a fast-moving environment with high standards and strong ownership, and know how to create that environment for the people you manage

 

The interview process

Round 1: First conversation to get to know you, understand what drives you, and explore why this role excites you.

Round 2: Two-part discussion where you’ll walk us through your career journey and the choices that shaped it, followed by a values-based interview.

Round 5: Final conversation with our founder.

jobs.title: Senior Engagement Manager, PS Sales - DACH
Senior Product Manager
jobs.description:
Getting homes off fossil fuels means fitting millions of heat pumps, solar panels and batteries, and every one has to be designed, sold and fitted by an installer. The assets themselves already work brilliantly, but getting them into homes is still slow, complex and painful. Our mission is to change that: to make it wildly easier and more profitable to run a renewables installation business, and get homes off fossil fuels way faster.

In just a few years we've become the leading platform for heat pump installers in the UK and Ireland, with around half of all heat pump installations now being managed on Spruce. We've just launched our solar and battery product, and we're building on that to go after even bigger opportunities: every other type of job these installers do, the rest of how they run their business, and a bunch of new countries.

We're now on the hunt for a truly brilliant Senior Product Manager to take ownership of massive chunks of the product: working out what installers need next, and getting it built beautifully and fast. You'll struggle to find a lovelier, more engaged group of customers to build for, or a more driven dev & design team to build with.

 

🌲 About Spruce

  • Almost 20% of the UK's carbon emissions comes from heating homes – there's simply no way to reach net zero without phasing out gas and oil boilers. Right now the only serious alternative is heat pumps, with their almost-magical ability to turn 1 kW of electricity into 3-5 kW of heat (🤯). But the heat pump installation journey is slow, inefficient, and just so painful. This makes it hard for existing installers to grow their businesses and puts off gas engineers from starting to do heat pumps. Perhaps most critically, it means you can't currently offer a heat pump when someone's boiler breaks and they urgently need heating.

  • We're fixing this. We've built a platform for heat pump installers to manage the whole installation journey from initial enquiry through to final compliance paperwork, freeing up their time to focus on what really matters: doing high-quality installations, providing great customer service, and scaling their business. Despite only getting started at the beginning of 2024, we're having a massive impact on installation businesses, suppliers, and manufacturers across the UK: halving the time they spend on each job and doubling their sales conversion rates.

  • We raised a chunky Seed round last year from top-tier investors and this year have doubled the team and grown revenue 4x. We've expanded into Ireland, have just launched an end-to-end solar and battery product, and are increasingly becoming the operating system for the whole home renewables supply chain. If you can picture a combination of ServiceTitan, Procore, and AutoCAD, you might get a sense of where we're headed…

 

🥖 The Role

Our initial success is due to putting our customers front-and-centre, rapidly building the tools that they need, and iterating based on their feedback. Your challenge is to ensure we maintain this deep understanding and the resulting customer love while massively expanding the range of problems we solve for our customers.

You'll work within a small product team, closely with our founders, and supported by a simply brilliant team of designers and developers. Day-to-day you'll be:

  • Leading discovery & user research – You'll design and run structured customer research to ensure we build the right things in the right order. You'll synthesise insights from user interviews, usage metrics and the commercial team, and use them to shape what we build.

  • Delivering features – You'll manage the build process all the way through to post-release testing. You'll work closely alongside devs & designers to bring features to life, ensuring we release quickly, maximise customer value and maintain product quality.

  • Reducing time-to-value – You'll help new users experience Spruce's value as soon as possible with minimal training, and partner with customer success to drive full platform adoption.

  • Monitoring & increasing impact – You'll measure the value generated for different customer types and identify opportunities to amplify our impact on their business.

  • Shaping company strategy – We're a deeply product-led business, so you'll be at the heart of shaping our future plans.

 

🫵 About You

We look for the same five things in everyone at Spruce: curiosity; intense drive, ambition and work ethic; a high degree of personal agency and ownership; deep humility and a growth mindset; and excellent craft.

You've likely got somewhere between 2 and 10 years' product management experience (we’re looking for excellent people and will scope the role based on your experience). You want to move fast and have a massive impact. On top of that, you're:

  • Highly structured & outcome-focused – You bring order to complex challenges, can synthesise information effectively, and take pride in well-documented processes. But while you love a good process, you ultimately care far more about delivering results and driving measurable outcomes;

  • Intellectually sharp & low ego – You quickly grasp new concepts, can explain complex ideas in simple terms, and (with a bit of help) can wrap your head around building physics, fluid dynamics, and dynamic tariff modelling. You're confident enough to push back when needed but humble enough to admit when you're wrong;

  • An exceptional communicator – You adapt your style to your audience, ask insightful questions, listen actively, and write clearly. You elevate any meeting and bring out the best in others;

  • Customer-obsessed – You genuinely care about fixing our users' problems and want to make technical tasks beautifully simple for even our least tech-savvy customers;

  • Already using AI intensively – You use it every day to make yourself disproportionately more effective, and you can show us how.

… and you'll hopefully also love heat pumps! 🤓

 

🌟 Our offer

  • 💰 £70–110k salary, depending on experience

  • 🍰 Equity (options) in the company

  • 🏡 Hybrid working: 3 days in-person a week (London or Bristol), with full-team meetups every fortnight

  • 🏖️ 33 days holiday (25 plus bank holidays) and opportunity to work from abroad for another 30 days each year

  • 🏥 Private Medical Cover (Vitality)

  • 👧 Workplace Nursery Benefit scheme (YellowNest)

  • 🧑‍🍼 Enhanced Parental Leave

  • 🚲 Cycle to Work scheme

  • 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Brilliant team to learn from and massive opportunity to grow

 

🧑‍💻 Working at Spruce

  • We're currently a close-knit team of 35, split between London and Bristol. We spend 2–3 days each week working together in-person in both locations, and get everyone together every fortnight.

  • You'll have genuine influence from day one. The best idea wins regardless of seniority. We expect you to challenge everything, ask "why?" multiple levels deep, and push back when something doesn't make sense.

  • We want everyone to spend time with installers on-site, feel their pain points, then rapidly suggest and implement solutions based on real feedback rather than assumptions. This is particularly important for this role, but you'll be surrounded by a whole team who are also close to our customers.

  • We move fast and ship imperfect things, learning from users rather than trying to perfect in isolation. When things break, we focus on how we fix it and what we can learn – and never blame. You'll own your outcomes whilst knowing the team has your back.

  • Feedback is constant, direct, and kind – we'll tell you when something isn't working and expect the same honesty (and empathy) back.

What Will You Be Doing?

Commission Processes

We need Marketing Ops leaders who can architect scalable systems, operate them strategically, and progressively embed AI into workflows — to raise quality, reduce manual execution, and unlock growth without scaling headcount linearly.

⭐️ The Marketing Ops job ⭐️

We are hiring two Marketing Operations Managers, each embedded in a different crew:

  • Growth Infrastructure — focused on prospect acquisition: building a unified lead engine that captures, scores, routes, and nurtures across all channels

  • Product Platform — focused on member lifecycle messaging: operating Alan's messaging stack as a scalable service across 1.7M+ profiles

Regardless of crew, you will own a core set of capabilities:

  • Data Model & Governance: maintain CRM data quality, attribute/event design, and database hygiene as a sustained practice

  • Segmentation & Lifecycle Design: design and maintain lifecycle stages, segmentation logic, routing rules, and re-engagement flows across multiple audiences and geos

  • Nurturing Infrastructure: own the nurturing stack and campaign processes; make launches autonomous and compliant

  • AI-First Operations: identify, build, and refine AI agents for email copywriting, lead scoring, next-best-action recommendations, and content generation — making marketers AI-powered, not replacing them

Product Platform — you'll operate Customer.io and back-end triggered emails as one governed system, monitor communication pressure and enforce channel rules, define and enforce recipient lifecycle paths, drive 100% Design Studio adoption, and co-own outbound messaging strategy with PMMs and product teams.

Outsight’s software solutions track the motion of people and vehicles using 3D LiDAR data.
Operators of transportation hubs like airports and train stations but also sport venues, road infrastructures and industrial sites can now access accurate and anonymous Spatial Intelligence data, in order to improve operations and increase user safety and satisfaction.
 
Our international team of scientists and engineers drive the development of our solutions from Paris, San Francisco, Sophia-Antipolis (Nice), Singapore & Hong Kong. To support our global outreach, we also operate a commercial office in Spain.
 
You can find below an interesting link about who we are and what we do :
Insights about Outsight
 
Our Passenger Flow Traffic Monitoring solution is trusted by the world’s leading airports and train stations across four continents, including the most renowned hubs celebrated for their operational excellence and exceptional passenger experience.  We also deploy our solutions in other markets such as Tourism, Retail and Sports.
Additionally, our Car Traffic Remote Monitoring product is trusted by several Tier 1 customers, including BMW.
 
 
Position Overview :
 
Outsight operates a Hybrid SaaS architecture and is shifting its operational focus from infrastructure-heavy systems support to application-level support. In this role, you maintain the daily stability of live customer deployments. You will isolate software incidents, parse application logs, and escalate verified product defects to the L2 Customer Engineering team. This position requires participating in a scheduled night and weekend on-call rotation.
 
What will be your responsibilities? 
 

  • Operational Handover: Validate that new customer deployments meet documentation, alert thresholds, and tracking metric standards before accepting operational ownership from Field Application Engineers (FAEs).

  • Technical Triaging: Triage incoming tickets, reproduce application defects in test environments, and escalate unresolved software issues to L2 engineering with targeted log data.

  • Production Operations: Execute scheduled configuration changes, system health audits, and remote software updates on live production environments.

  • Documentation: Write and maintain internal runbooks and technical troubleshooting guides to standardize incident resolution workflows.

  • Root Cause Analysis (RCA): Reconstruct incident timelines and extract log data to submit bug reports to Product and Engineering teams.

 
What are the requirements for the role? 
 

  • Experience: 3+ years supporting live production software environments within technical support, system administration, deployment engineering, or site reliability engineering (SRE).

  • Linux Skills: Direct experience with Linux/Unix command-line navigation, system administration utilities, log parsing, and remote diagnostics.

  • Infrastructure & Networking: Experience navigating hybrid environments combining physical hardware, TCP/IP networking (DNS, VPNs, firewalls, VLANs), and cloud services.

  • Incident Communication: Experience providing technical timelines and status updates to internal stakeholders during critical incidents.

  • Languages: Professional fluency in English. French language proficiency is an asset.

  • Flexibility: Availability to participate in a scheduled night and weekend on-call rotation.

  • Preferred Qualifications: Hands-on experience with Bash, Python, SQL, REST APIs, Docker, Kubernetes, Grafana, or Prometheus. Background in IoT, edge computing, or computer vision environments.

 
Why join us?
 

Be part of the team pioneering Spatial Intelligence solutions at unprecedented scale—the breakthrough technology transforming how the world’s most prestigious airports, infrastructure operators, and smart cities understand and optimize physical flows.

As a 7-time Gartner-recognized category-defining leader with dozens of global awards including “Edge AI Product of the Year,” “LiDAR Leader Award,” “CES Best of Innovation” and many more, we’re backed by 37 patents and deployments with the most prestigious (and challenging) customers across four continents.

Join our international team of world-class experienced engineers and business leaders solving humanity’s most complex spatial challenges, from passenger flow optimization to autonomous robotics coordination, while working at the cutting edge of 3D AI, LiDAR perception, and real-time analytics.

Supported by rock-solid investors including BNP Paribas, BPI France, Energy Innovation Capital and Demeter who back our long-term vision, this is your opportunity to shape how physical and digital worlds interact, with the resources, growth trajectory, and technical challenges that will accelerate your career in ways traditional companies cannot offer.

jobs.title: Commissions & Targets Manager
jobs.description:
About Us

Perk (formerly TravelPerk) is the intelligent platform for travel and spend management. Built to tackle the time-consuming, manual work that gets in the way of real work, our tools automate everything from travel bookings to expenses, invoice processing, and more. By eliminating this shadow work that wastes hours, erodes morale, and saps innovation, we're on a mission to power real work, with real impact.

We're trusted by more than 12,000 companies worldwide, including Bolt, GoCardless, and Fabletics, and we're tackling the 7 hours of lost productivity per employee each week, a $1.7 trillion problem.

Founded in 2015, Perk has grown into a global company of more than 1,800 people across 12 offices globally, with headquarters in London and Boston. We combine innovation, control, and simplicity to transform how businesses work and how people feel at work.

At Perk, we're driven by our values, like being an owner, delivering a 7-star experience, and working as one team. We value curiosity, purpose, and mindset, not just knowledge, to unlock the power in your potential. Our talent team brings together leading minds from the travel, fintech, and SaaS industries, representing over 70 countries. If you're excited about having a real impact and shaping how millions of people experience work, we'd love you on the team.

Visit www.perk.com to learn more.

The Role

We're looking for a Commissions & Targets Manager to own how our sales organisation is paid and how its targets are set. You'll run the commission process end to end, manage CaptivateIQ, handle complex cases, and run the quarterly target distribution for our sales reps. You'll shape our commission strategy with the Director of Revenue Operations.

You'll also be the go-to person for two experienced commission analysts. It's not a line management role, but you'll guide the team on difficult cases. Payouts depend on accurate numbers delivered on fixed deadlines, so we need someone with strong attention to detail who prioritises well in a fast-moving team.

This is an Individual Contributor role.


What You'll Do

  • First 90 days: Master our commission plans, workflows, and CaptivateIQ setup, and execute your first end-of-quarter close with support from the Director.

  • First 6 months: Take full ownership of the end-of-quarter close and case escalations, and lead your first quarterly target distribution.

  • First 12 months: Partner with the Director to shape our commission strategy while optimising the processes and system configurations you inherited.


What Will You Be Doing?

Commission Processes

  • Manage the end-of-quarter commission process, from data validation and plan calculations to review, approvals and payout handover. Start with the Director's oversight and take full ownership of the process within your first two quarters.

  • Define the end-of-quarter schedule: map all the activities, decide which to prioritise, identify what can be front-loaded ahead of quarter end, and build a plan that hits the deadlines and delivers quality results.

  • During the close, make quick calls and reprioritise when things go wrong, flag risks before they affect payouts, and keep the process documented and auditable.

  • Spot recurring errors and bottlenecks, and fix them at the source.

Commission Cases & Team Support

  • Act as the escalation point for complex or disputed commission cases, supporting the two commission analysts.

  • Coach the analysts on case handling, resolve difficult cases and make clear, consistent and well-documented decisions.

  • Identify patterns in the cases raised, and use them to improve plan rules, documentation and communication.

Commission System Ownership

  • Manage our commissions system, CaptivateIQ: plan configuration, data integrations, quarterly updates and access.

  • Partner with the Sales Operations, Finance and Data team on data quality and any system changes.

  • Test and validate changes before each close, so that calculations are accurate and reproducible.

Commission Strategy

  • Work with the Director of Revenue Operations to define the commission strategy, including plan design, rules and how they support company goals.

  • Analyse plan performance and its effect on sales behaviour, and bring a point of view on what to change.

  • Prepare the commission plan updates for each planning period and communicate them clearly to sales and finance stakeholders.

Quarterly Target Distribution

  • Run the target setting cycle each quarter, with clear methodology and timelines, and explain the outcomes to sales leaders.

  • Make sure any outlier or special case target adjustments are handled before the targets are published.

  • Handle target questions and adjustments in a fair and consistent way.


What Will You Need to Succeed?

  • Strong experience in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, Sales Compensation or a similar role, preferably in a SaaS or technology company operating at a global or European level.

  • Hands-on experience running commission processes for a quota-carrying sales organisation, including end-of-quarter closes.

  • Experience administering a commissions system (CaptivateIQ or a similar tool such as Qobra) is preferred but not required.

  • Exceptional attention to detail and the discipline to deliver accurate results on fixed deadlines.

  • A strong ability to improve processes: you spot what is manual, error-prone or slow, and fix it at the source.

  • Ability to prioritise well and make fast, accurate calls in a fast-moving, deadline-driven environment.

  • Strong analytical skills. Experience setting or contributing to sales targets and quotas is a plus.

  • Good judgment and strong stakeholder management, including handling sensitive conversations about pay with sales leaders, finance and ICs.

  • Experience guiding or coaching other analysts.

  • Clear written and verbal communication in English.

  • Experience working with global or multi-region teams is a plus.

What We Offer?

  • 25 days of annual leave to rest and recharge, plus all public holidays.

  • An optional pension scheme to support your long-term financial wellbeing.

  • A tax-efficient bike leasing scheme through Lease a Bike, for your commute or personal use.

  • Reimbursed commuting costs if you live more than 10km away from the office.

  • Competitive compensation paired with equity in Perk.

  • Unforgettable team experiences, including our annual summer party.

  • Comprehensive wellbeing support through Spring Health, offering fast access to 12 therapy and 12 coaching sessions for you and your loved ones.

  • Focus on your family with 12-16 weeks’ paid parental leave

  • 16 paid volunteer hours each year to give back to causes you care about.

  • Up to 20 “Work From Anywhere” days annually to explore the world while staying connected.

  • A fully paid four-week sabbatical after five years with Perk.

  • Relocation support to help you move seamlessly into one of our hubs.

AI at Perk
AI is embedded in how we work across every function. The tools you'll use day-to-day are AI-enabled so you can move faster and spend more time on the work that matters. In practice, that means using AI to research and prioritise accounts, draft and refine outreach, handle customer interactions more effectively, synthesise information, and cut through shadow work - the invisible tasks that pull people away from the work only they can do - so you can focus on relationships and outcomes.

How We Work

At Perk, we take an IRL-first approach to work, where our team works together in-person 3 days a week. As such, this role requires you to be based within commuting distance of our hubs. We fundamentally believe in the value of meeting in real life to improve connectivity, productivity, creativity and ultimately making us a great place to work.

For certain roles, we can help with relocation from anywhere in the world, English is the official language at the office. Please submit your resume in English if you choose to apply. Do not forget to submit an updated portfolio and/or resume.

Perk is a global company with a diverse customer base, and we want to make sure the people behind our product reflect that. We’re an equal opportunity employer, which means you’re welcome at Perk regardless of how you look, where you’re from, or anything else that makes you, well, you.

Protect Yourself from Recruitment Scams

All official communication from Perk will always come from email addresses ending in @perk.com or @externalperk.com, our verified social media channels, or recruiters listed on our official LinkedIn page. We will never ask you to pay for equipment, training, or fees, request sensitive personal information such as bank details early in the process, or communicate through unofficial apps like WhatsApp, Telegram, or Signal. If you receive a message claiming to be from Perk that seems suspicious, please do not respond. Forward it to security [at] perk .com, and we will confirm whether it is legitimate.

jobs.title: Business Operations Intern – New HQ Project Lead (m/f/d)
jobs.description:
Our Mission

At Omegga, we develop spectral intelligence: we combine AI and spectroscopy to make the invisible visible. We started with a clear objective: eliminate chick culling on a global scale through early, non-invasive in-ovo sex detection. This outdated practice still impacts billions of lives, and we're here to change that. We're not building for the niche; we're building for the global standard.

Today, our technology is the world's earliest commercially available in-ovo sex determination and is already running in live production. As a B2B company, we work directly with hatcheries, and our focus is on scaling performance, robustness, and deployment across an international customer base. Beyond this first application, our platform enables non-invasive material analysis across biological and industrial environments, from agriculture to food production and beyond.

Since closing our €10 million funding round in early 2026 (including IQ Capital, Capnamic and the EIC Fund), our team has quickly doubled to 30 people, bringing together expertise in AI, optics and industrial systems.

We are looking for people who take ownership, think in systems, and want to help turn a working product into the industry benchmark. If that sounds like you, we'd love to hear from you.

Your Mission

We're building our new headquarter, and we need someone to own it. Your challenge: build a fully operational home of a fast-growing deep-tech company from scratch. This isn't an internship where you support someone else's project. This one is yours.

  • Own the HQ Build-out: Drive the project from the first plan to the day the doors open: flooring, cabling, furniture and everything in between.

  • Bring People Together: Coordinate internal teams, contractors and service providers, collect quotes, and keep timelines and budget on track. On site, you're the go-to person.

  • Set Up Our Deep-Tech Hardware: Plan material needs and procurement, and work hand in hand with our engineering team to get our in-house hardware up and running.

  • Write Your Own Playbook: There's no template for this. Challenge assumptions, spot opportunities and find pragmatic solutions when plans meet reality.

  • Cross-functional Support: Beyond the HQ, help translate business updates into clear stakeholder communication in investor relation HR, PR and sales.

Why Us

  • Work That Matters: You're not optimizing ad clicks. You're helping a company that is ending chick culling in hatcheries today, and expanding AI-powered spectroscopy far beyond it.

  • Fair Compensation: A properly paid, full-time internship, because real work deserves real pay.

  • Team & Workplace: A team of 30 with short decision paths, currently based in Munich's Werksviertel and soon in the new headquarters you'll help build. We work hard, stay focused, and get things done together on site.

  • Perks Budget: Monthly budget to spend where it actually matters to you: fitness, mobility, or the occasional "I earned this" purchase.

  • Office: Free drinks, coffee, and snacks to keep you focused throughout the day.

Your Profile

Requirements: German at C1 level or higher, fluent English, and a valid class B driver's license for quick supply runs, whether to IKEA or the hardware store.

Beyond that, we care more about how you think, act and take ownership than about a perfect CV.

  • Confident communicator: You're comfortable with contractors, engineers, suppliers and senior stakeholders alike. You articulate your perspective clearly and challenge assumptions constructively.

  • Execution-driven: You follow through and care about outcomes, not just activity. No task is beneath you, and speed never comes at the expense of quality.

  • Independent & resourceful: You don't need a detailed roadmap to get started. You structure your own work, find the information you need, and know when to involve others.

  • Structured & pragmatic: You break complex problems into manageable steps, prioritize effectively, and keep track of budgets, deadlines and dependencies. When information is incomplete, you weigh the trade-offs, make a pragmatic call, and adapt when circumstances change.

  • Intellectually curious: You grasp new concepts quickly, ask the right questions, and enjoy figuring out things you haven't done before.

  • Entrepreneurial mindset: You see opportunities where others see problems. You take initiative, turn ideas into action, and when you see a chance to build or improve something, you have the room to pitch it and make it your own.

  • Self-reflective: You actively seek feedback, own your mistakes, and keep improving how you work.

Nice to have: Experience in project management, operations, procurement, entrepreneurship or coordinating external partners. Your mindset and potential matter more to us.

WHY THIS ROLE IS DIFFERENT

  • Tangible Impact: At the end of your internship, you can walk through our new headquarter and say: I built this.

  • Real Ownership: A business-critical project that's yours from start to finish.

  • Steep Learning Curve: Grow fast across entrepreneurship, project management and business operations, and learn to work with contractors, engineers and investors alike.

  • Real Responsibility: Real budgets, real negotiations, real operational decisions.

  • Freedom to Shape: Build your own approach instead of following predefined processes.

  • Founder Exposure: Work directly with the founding team of a venture-backed deep-tech company.

  • Insights into Deep Tech: See how a deep-tech startup sets up its hardware infrastructure and works with its investors.

About Us

Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies is a joint venture between two industry leaders with a clear vision for automotive’s next chapter. From operating systems to zonal controllers to cloud and connectivity solutions, we’re addressing the challenges of electric vehicles through technology that will set the standards for software-defined vehicles around the world.

The road to the future is uncharted. By combining our expertise across connectivity, AI, security and more, we’ll map a new way forward. Working together, we’ll create a future that’s more connected, more intelligent, more sustainable for everyone.

Role Summary

The Berlin team is looking for a Staff Software Engineer - Infotainment, to provide hands-on technical leadership for complex embedded software and hardware/software integration work. You will help shape architectures that connect vehicle hardware, embedded operating systems, platform services, communication paths, and user-facing behavior into reliable products.

This is a broad technical role for an engineer who can move comfortably between system-level design and implementation. You will work across current and next-generation vehicle platforms, helping teams take ideas from early architecture through development, integration, validation, and production readiness. You’ll be working in a high-performing forward-deployed team working closely with key OEM stakeholders. Examples include physical input, HMI systems and bespoke in-vehicle touchpoints.

This role is based in our Berlin office and requires a minimum of three days per week onsite.

Responsibilities

  • Architect, design, develop, and maintain embedded software across hardware interfaces, operating-system services, middleware, communication paths, and applications, using C/C++ and contributing to Rust adoption where it improves safety, reliability, maintainability, or service boundaries.

  • Lead technical design discussions and translate ambiguous requirements into clear interfaces, ownership boundaries, acceptance criteria, dependencies, delivery plans, reusable abstractions, and configuration contracts that scale across vehicle platforms, products, and variants.

  • Evaluate and optimize constrained systems for CPU, memory, storage, power, latency, startup, concurrency, and fault handling while ensuring predictable behavior, reliability, and maintainability.

  • Guide the integration of hardware-linked behavior—including physical controls, display interaction, vehicle signals, persistent state, device configuration, and other time-sensitive system behavior—across software and hardware components.

  • Lead complex software and hardware investigations and drive end-to-end validation using logs, traces, diagnostics, target hardware, laboratory equipment, simulators, emulators, software-in-the-loop, hardware-in-the-loop, and prototype vehicles.

  • Partner with hardware, firmware, platform, application, validation, product, and external teams to resolve dependencies and make timely technical decisions; establish practices for schemas, generated bindings, diagnostics, observability, versioning, compatibility, and maintainability; and mentor engineers while communicating architecture, risks, trade-offs, and decisions clearly.

Qualifications

  • Strong hands-on experience developing, debugging, reviewing, and maintaining C and/or C++ software, with practical Rust experience or the ability and interest to learn Rust.

  • Experience with embedded operating systems, embedded Linux, real-time systems, board-support packages, device drivers, hypervisor-based systems, or comparable constrained computing environments.

  • Strong understanding of hardware/software interfaces, communication protocols, concurrency, timing, startup and reset behavior, resource constraints, fault handling, and system performance across CPU, power, memory, storage, latency, reliability, and degraded operation.

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer, Vehicle Configuration Platform
jobs.description:
About Us

Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies is a joint venture between two industry leaders with a clear vision for automotive’s next chapter. From operating systems to zonal controllers to cloud and connectivity solutions, we’re addressing the challenges of electric vehicles through technology that will set the standards for software-defined vehicles around the world.

The road to the future is uncharted. By combining our expertise across connectivity, AI, security and more, we’ll map a new way forward. Working together, we’ll create a future that’s more connected, more intelligent, more sustainable for everyone.

Role Summary

A single firmware release must serve every vehicle variant we build across both Rivian and all Volkswagen brands. The vehicle configuration platform that the OTA team supports makes that possible: a schema-driven system that defines every configurable attribute of a vehicle and provisions them onto vehicles in the factory, in service, and over the air customer updates. Getting this wrong can mean anything from the wrong information showing on the driver display to a car that needs to be towed in for service.

You will be a technical leader on the team that owns this platform, working as a peer to its lead architect. Where the architect drives the structural evolution of the configuration system itself, you will own the health, reliability, and scalability of everything around it: the compilation and code generation pipelines, the validation and release infrastructure, the provisioning path from schema to vehicle, and the developer experience of every engineer who touches configuration. You will set technical direction for this surface area, drive initiatives that span firmware, build infrastructure, release engineering, OTA, and factory integration across two companies' engineering organizations, and raise the bar for how the team designs, reviews, and ships.

This role is based in our Berlin office and requires a minimum of three days per week onsite, with occasional travel to other company and partner sites as needed.

 

Responsibilities

  • Own the technical direction for configuration tooling, validation, and delivery infrastructure, translating platform architecture into a concrete, sequenced roadmap and driving it to completion across teams.

  • Lead initiatives that simplify the platform: consolidating redundant mechanisms, retiring legacy pathways, and reducing the coordination cost of routine changes, while every downstream consumer keeps working.

  • Design the compatibility strategy for data contracts deployed to devices in the field, and build the automated enforcement that makes schema evolution provably safe rather than carefully reviewed.

  • Architect the validation and release pipeline as a product: define what classes of defects must be impossible to merge, and build the layered checks, staged rollouts, and observability that get there.

  • Serve as the senior escalation point for production configuration issues, leading root cause analysis during launches and field events and converting each incident into systemic prevention.

  • Drive alignment across organizational boundaries, negotiating shared contracts, review processes, and release mechanics with firmware, cloud, diagnostics, manufacturing, and partner-brand stakeholders who have differing constraints and conventions.

  • Mentor and multiply the engineers on the team, setting standards through design review, raising the quality of technical writing and decision records, and growing the mid-level engineers toward ownership.

  • Be accountable for the long-term maintenance cost of what the team ships.

 

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of software engineering experience, including demonstrated ownership of a platform, infrastructure, or developer-facing system used by many teams.

  • A track record of leading cross-team technical initiatives from proposal through delivery, including ones that required deprecating or migrating away from entrenched systems.

  • Deep experience with serialization formats such as Protocol Buffers, including designing schemas with strict backward and forward compatibility guarantees for devices you cannot force-update.

  • Strong Python and working C literacy; real depth in a modern build system such as Bazel, including writing rules and repository-level integration, not just consuming builds.

  • Mature CI/CD and release engineering judgment: you design validation gates and rollout mechanics that encode correctness in automation, and you know which guarantees belong in tooling versus process.

About the role

Electronics is a trillion-dollar industry that still runs on spreadsheets, email threads and part-search tabs. Luminovo is the AI platform that replaces them, and DACH is our home market, with 400+ customers worldwide.

We're adding an Account Executive to our German-speaking team. You will sell our procurement intelligence platform to OEMs, from automotive suppliers to industrial equipment and medical device makers: procurement, supply chain and engineering leaders who want to cut component costs and see supply risk before it stops production. Our buyers rarely arrive knowing they have a problem worth solving, so you win through deep discovery, a sharp business case and trust built across several stakeholders.

You will write the playbook with us. Our OEM motion in DACH is still being built, and you will shape how we sell to it, with a founder and a VP of Sales next to you.

 

Your performance objectives

Generate pipeline

  • Create qualified pipeline of roughly €420k–€500k ARR per quarter at Level 2 and €570k–€680k at Level 3, through your own outbound, events and the meetings our BDRs book, qualified with SPICED (Situation, Pain, Impact, Critical event, Decision criteria).

  • Build your network: connect with 50+ relevant decision-makers at electronics manufacturers per quarter and represent Luminovo at 2–3 industry fairs a year.

  • Ramp with clear targets: in your first 3 months, complete the discovery and demo certifications and all Lumiversity courses, and create 4 qualified opportunities at Level 2 or 6 at Level 3 (6 and 9 with BDR support). In your second quarter you work toward 50% of full quota, and from there toward full quota.

Close opportunities

  • Run demos tailored to each customer's pain and prove value with domain experts in workshops that quantify ROI: savings against market prices, risk exposure uncovered, disruptions avoided.

  • Guide prospects through complex buyer journeys: map stakeholders, handle procurement and legal, close about €105k–€125k of new ARR per quarter at Level 2 or €143k–€169k at Level 3, and hand over smoothly to Customer Success.

Build your OEM playbook

  • Within 6 months, document what works in the DACH OEM segment (messaging, discovery questions, objections) and contribute it to our sales playbook.

  • Feed customer and market insight to Product every month, with at least one concrete product input that lands on the roadmap.

Lead by example

  • Own your metrics (pipeline health, conversion, deal velocity) and use them to hit your quarterly targets.

  • Mentor our BDRs through call reviews and shared discovery, and ask for coaching after every major customer interaction.

 

Your potential growth path

  • Months 1–6: master the product, close your first 5–10 deals, build your DACH network.

  • Months 6–18: take on larger deals and complex stakeholder setups, mentor BDRs.

  • 18+ months: move into Enterprise AE (€100k+ deals), own strategic accounts, mentor junior AEs.

 

Your territory and work setup

German-speaking market (DACH) plus some English-speaking territories. Discovery, demos and negotiations happen in German and the company works in English, so you need both at a professional level. Hybrid at our Munich HQ or Berlin hub, with the sales team in the office three days a week. Occasional travel for retreats and industry events, costs covered.

 

Whom you'll be working with

  • Clifton Lobo, VP Global Sales, your manager, who coaches you on deal strategy and career progression

  • Sebastian Schaal, co-founder, for positioning and pricing

  • Inga Schwarz, Team Lead and pioneer AE for OEM, your partner in building the OEM playbook

  • Dasha and our BDR team, who feed you qualified meetings

  • Max Hungenbach and RevOps for CRM, dashboards and enablement

  • Marketing and Customer Success

 

Why Luminovo

  • Measurable product impact: our procurement intelligence shows OEMs where they pay above market and which parts put production at risk, so your business case starts from the customer's own BOMs

  • An open field: you shape the DACH OEM playbook with a founder and our VP Global Sales next to you

  • AI is part of how we work, from our MCP integrations to the agents our own teams build

  • Psychological safety, honest feedback, an international and remote-first team

If you're interested to find out more about why we banned requirements from our performance profiles – see here.

 

⚡️ About Luminovo

Luminovo is the first electronics supply chain platform that unites all data, processes, and stakeholders in the trillion-dollar electronics industry.

We fundamentally believe that technology is the best tool that humankind has developed to tackle the biggest challenges we face as a society today. And we want to do our share in accelerating technological progress.

We bring innovations to life faster and cheaper by creating a more connected and resilient electronics supply chain.

To date, over 400 active customers worldwide are working with us towards this shared goal. Supported by leading investors such as Cherry Ventures, General Catalyst/LaFamiglia, Chalfen Ventures, and others, we have raised more than €20 million.

Our core principles: putting people first & building great things

Our team includes a mix of product enthusiasts, people advocates, business masterminds, and engineering experts. We provide an authentic environment based on psychological safety to empower Luminerds from various backgrounds to succeed, grow, and focus on impact. Putting people first means that we deeply care about who our employees are, what makes them unique, and what they excel at.

jobs.description:
adjoe is redefining the future of mobile ads. Powered by advanced AI, first-party data and world-class engineers, we’ve perfected the offerwall experience for monetizing and scaling app publishers with solutions like Playtime and Arcade – now the fastest growing rewarded advertising channel globally – driving incremental engagement, retention, and revenue.

At the same time, we’re breaking into programmatic advertising with the intelligent bidding system of adjoe Ads. Together, this ecosystem connects app developers to over 600 million users worldwide for scalable growth. Backed by a $100 million investment from Bertelsmann and operating from offices in Hamburg, Boston, Singapore, and Tokyo, adjoe is defining the next stages of app and ad experience – right now. Our Rewarded Solutions team develops the technology behind adjoe’s innovative rewarded engagement products that serve over 57 million daily mobile users.

The team’s tech stack consists of three major components: native Android and iOS SDKs written in Java/Kotlin and Swift handling complex engagement flows; widely customizable offerwall applications built with React TypeScript; and a highly performant Golang backend hosted on AWS that processes millions of events hourly. Our system matches each game with its ideal users, delivering rewards optimized for satisfaction through data processed via AWS Athena, Kafka, Spark, S3, and MySQL.

For team members, this means having state-of-the-art resources to build engaging rewarded ad experiences that seamlessly integrate into the world’s top apps while delivering exceptional results for advertisers and monetizers in this industry-leading technology.

What you will do:

  • Manage the technical onboarding of our app partners in EMEA onto our new solution, ensuring a smooth SDK implementation process.

  • Partner with advertisers as a trusted technical advisor, helping them shape their technical strategy, overcome challenges, and identify opportunities to achieve their business goals.

  • Support advertisers with integration issues, ranging from debugging mobile app code to fine-tuning configurations, and proactively identify recurring issues and work with Product and Engineering to develop solutions.

  • Support the demand business team with data-driven insights to help publishers achieve their KPIs, and partner with Growth Managers to prepare impactful Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) that identify opportunities for revenue growth.

  • Contribute to product ideation and drive product improvements by translating customer and support team feedback into actionable solutions.

  • Maintain clear, easy-to-understand documentation of the integration process.

  • Collaborate with an international, English-speaking team dedicated to scaling our adtech platform beyond hundreds of millions of monthly active users.

Who you are:

  • You have 3+ years of experience in a technical client-facing role in AdTech, Big Tech, or SaaS (TAM, Sales Engineering, or Solutions Architecture), with some exposure to the mobile ecosystem.

  • You can break down complex technical concepts into clear, easy-to-understand explanations for business teams and partners in English.

  • You have strong analytical and communication skills, can turn data into actionable insights, and are comfortable using SQL to query databases.

  • You understand how technical systems communicate, including how to test HTTP REST endpoints and troubleshoot common integration issues.

  • You have a curious mindset and are comfortable asking questions to challenge assumptions and uncover root causes.

  • You take initiative and have a strong bias toward action. You proactively identify gaps, think critically about potential solutions, and take ownership of driving improvements rather than waiting for others to act.

  • Fluency in English

  • Plus: A software engineering background and experience with Java and app development.

  • Huge plus: You have hands-on experience supporting advertisers through SDK integrations, ideally in the mobile gaming space, debugging complex issues, and guiding them on best practices for smooth rollouts and long-term success.

  • Location: Based in Hamburg

🌎 We welcome applications from talent worldwide and provide relocation support to Hamburg, Germany for those ready to join our team.

What’s in It for You?
At adjoe, we are not just managing campaigns, we're helping build the business engine behind one of the fastest-growing adtech platforms in mobile. We are proactively curious: we question status quo, think outside the box, connect the dots. The partnerships you close, the strategies you execute, and the markets you develop will directly shape how adjoe scales globally.

We recently raised our Series A from leading US and European investors and software operators. We’re now entering our next chapter: investing heavily in product and AI, expanding internationally, and building the team that can make Dotfile the global standard for compliance infrastructure.

About the role

You’ll join an AI-native engineering team where AI is central to how we design, build and ship software. We’re looking for a Senior Software Engineer who understands software deeply, uses AI to build better software faster, and wants to help improve how the whole team works.

You will own projects from understanding the customer problem to shipping a solution and improving it in production. Working closely with engineering and product, you will help decide what we build, how we build it, and where to invest as the platform grows.

This is a hands-on role with broad ownership. Your focus will reflect your strengths and the team’s priorities, whether that means building product experiences, developing backend services, or solving challenges across the platform. We value engineers who bring depth in their area and curiosity beyond it.

What you’ll do

  • Own projects from discovery and technical design through implementation, testing, deployment and follow-up.

  • Work closely with product and other engineers to understand customer needs, challenge assumptions and turn complex requirements into clear, usable software.

  • Build and improve the interfaces, APIs and services that financial institutions rely on for their compliance operations.

  • Make pragmatic technical decisions, balancing delivery speed with reliability, security and maintainability.

  • Investigate production issues and improve performance, observability and resilience as the platform grows.

  • Raise the engineering bar through knowledge sharing and improvements to how we develop and ship software.

  • Contribute to the evolution of our platform as we build more AI-powered compliance capabilities.

About you

  • You have 5+ years of software engineering experience, with a track record of delivering and maintaining software in production.

  • You understand software in depth. You bring strong fundamentals and depth in backend or full-stack development. You can reason about data, concurrency, performance and failure modes, and investigate unfamiliar systems beyond the surface.

  • AI coding agents are central to how you work. You use tools such as Codex or Claude Code extensively to explore, build, test and review software. You keep experimenting with ways to make yourself more effective.

  • You bring the judgment that makes AI-assisted development work. You frame problems clearly, provide useful context, challenge assumptions and verify the resulting behavior. You can explain why a solution works and take responsibility for what you ship.

  • You take ownership. You can turn an ambiguous problem into a practical plan, follow through on delivery and improve the result in production. You are comfortable learning new technologies and working beyond your usual area when a problem calls for it.

  • You care about the product as much as the implementation. You want to understand who you are building for, challenge requirements when needed and assess whether your work solves the original problem.

  • You value simple, well-designed solutions. You know when to move quickly and when reliability, security or long-term maintenance require more care.

  • You communicate clearly in English and enjoy collaborating. You explain your technical choices, welcome constructive disagreement and share what you learn with your teammates.

  • You want to help shape an AI-native engineering team. You enjoy improving how software gets built, from reusable agent workflows to better testing and feedback loops, and turning your own discoveries into practices that make the whole team more effective.

Experience in B2B SaaS, fintech or compliance is a plus.

Our technology

Our main language is TypeScript. Our stack includes:

  • Frontend: React, Apollo GraphQL and Storybook.

  • Backend: Node.js, NestJS, GraphQL and PostgreSQL.

  • Infrastructure: AWS and Kubernetes.

  • Development and testing: Nx, GitLab CI, Playwright.

You do not need experience with every part of our stack. We care about your engineering judgment, your ability to learn and the quality of the software you build.

Why join us

  • Join a company with traction and room to shape its future. With 100+ financial institutions using Dotfile and a recent Series A, you’ll help define the next stage of the product and engineering team.

  • Help shape how an AI-native team works. Experiment with new approaches, improve your own workflow and turn what you learn into practices that make the whole team more effective.

  • Put your engineering depth to work. Solve demanding problems in automation, AI, data and reliability, building software that financial institutions depend on every day.

  • Have a direct say in what you build. Influence technical decisions, own projects through to production, and see how your work changes the customer experience.


Our hiring process

  1. CTO conversation — 30-60 minutes : Discuss your background, explore the role and how our engineering team works, and answer technical questions to assess your engineering knowledge and problem-solving approach.

  2. Case study — 60 minutes : Design the architecture of a project we provide, or present the architecture of a past project you led. Walk us through your reasoning, technical decisions and trade-offs.

  3. Raise the bar — 30 minutes: Meet someone from Product or Solutions Consulting to discuss how you collaborate across teams, understand customer needs and approach problems together.

  4. Founder discussion — 15-30 minutes: Meet our CEO to discuss Dotfile’s ambition, what motivates you and the contribution you could make.

jobs.title: Clinical Lead, Women's Health
jobs.description:
Health can’t wait.

Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t.

Alan exists to end the wait.

Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way.

So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience.

We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture. We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR.

Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond.

💜 The role

Women's bodies are different, yet medicine still treats them the same. Women get diagnosed about 4 years later than men on average across 700+ types of disease. In France, 51% of women say a health professional has played down their symptoms at least once.

We want to change that. We are building the health system women never had: one that listens to women, anticipates their needs at every stage of life instead of waiting for problems to appear, and gives them care they can trust. To do this, we combine the latest evidence, digital tools, AI and carefully selected health professionals with our strength as an insurer.

We are looking for a doctor who wants to do medicine differently: to build products that thousands of women use and that address their needs; to move care towards prevention; and to work every day with people who think differently, such as product managers, designers, engineers and marketers.

As our Clinical Lead for Women's Health, you make this clinically credible and effective. You own the clinical choices, and you are an essential and active contributor in the product team.

A few things to know before you apply

  • This is a clinical role inside a product team, at an early stage. You own the clinical choices and you build the product with project builder, engineers, designers, ... A good product combines many factors, and the clinical side is one of them. There is a lot to build, to test and to change, and not everything is proven yet. For example, we measure how much our services are used much better than the health outcomes they achieve: building that measurement, honestly, is part of the job.

  • You work outside the usual medical world. Most of your colleagues are not health professionals. You will confront perspectives, explain clinical constraints in simple words, listen to product and business constraints, and find solutions together. Decisions are discussed and made as a team.

  • It takes real time. We prefer 80% or more; at least 60% is possible.

What you will do

You will be the clinical lead of our Women's Health offer, and you will help turn it into a product that women use and trust.

  • Build the product with the team. Work closely with product managers, designers and engineers, and bring the clinical view early, when it shapes decisions, not at the end. With AI tools, you can also build simple things yourself, without knowing how to code.

  • Own the clinical choices. Define our clinical positions based on evidence, design protocols and care pathways, and hold a few clear, explained red lines. When something doesn't work, you help find a safe and relevant alternative.

  • Make our AI safe and accurate on women's health. Work with the product team on how Mo, our AI-powered health companion, handles women's health topics, and help evaluate and improve it.

  • Show the value for women. Help define how we measure the impact on women's health, using evidence-based tools and value-based healthcare principles.

  • Work with our Clinic team. Work hand in hand with Alan's doctors, midwives and other health professionals: help train and support them, and be the person they turn to for difficult cases.

  • Feed and endorse our medical communication. Make sure what we say about women's health is accurate and evidence-based, and help explain it in simple words. Over time, you may represent Alan on these topics.

What success looks like in 6 months

  • Product: you are a core member of the product team, and the first member journeys reflect your clinical input from the start.

  • Protocols in use: the clinical protocols and care pathways of our first women's health program are validated and applied by the Clinic team.

  • Clinic team: midwives and doctors on the program are trained on the protocols, clinical staffing is under way, and you supervise complex cases.

  • Health outcomes: the program's health outcomes are defined and tracked.

  • AI quality: you have helped us make sure our AI handles women's health safely and accurately.

What this role is not

  • Not a medical advisor or reviewer who comes in at the end, nor the person who decides alone.

  • Not the person who runs all the consultations: our midwives and doctors do that, and you design, pilot and supervise.

  • Not an expert on every topic: you bring in other health professionals when needed.

A dynamic, international community of health professionals

You don't work alone. You join Alan's health professionals community: a large network of doctors, midwives, psychologists and other clinicians in France, Spain, Belgium and Canada, and a small core team of Alaners, other clinical leads working on different health programs or services. It is a community with high standards, direct and caring feedback, and a lot of room to shape things.

Beyond Women's Health, you will:

  • Share your practice and learn from others through case reviews and community sessions;

  • Help set common standards across programs;

  • Help welcome, train and mentor new health professionals joining Alan;

  • Help other teams at Alan understand key health concepts, such as evidence-based care;

  • Over time, contribute to other health topics beyond Women's Health.

👀 Is it you we're looking for?

Must-haves

  • You are a gynecologist (OB-GYN) or a GP with solid training in women's health, for example a university diploma (DU or DIU) in gynecology, or several years of regular gynecological follow-up in your practice. You can come from private practice, a hospital, a clinic or a health tech company.

  • At least 5 years of post-residency experience, with solid clinical judgment and evidence-based prescribing.

  • Clinical experience across several areas of women's health, for example contraception, fertility, endometriosis, menopause or hormone treatments.

  • An open, pragmatic mindset: you enjoy working with non-medical teams, you make trade-offs when they are legitimate while defending evidence-based rigor, and you are curious about what AI and digital tools change in medicine.

  • Outcomes thinking: you care about the results that matter to patients compared with what care costs (value-based healthcare), and about prevention, not only treatment.

  • A great understanding of the French healthcare system.

  • Fluency in both French and English.

Nice-to-haves

  • Experience training or supervising other health professionals is a plus, and a collaborative approach with midwives, dietitians, therapists, …

  • Experience in digital health, a start-up, a healthcare project or teleconsultation.

  • Experience writing or contributing to a clinical protocol or guideline.

🤝 How we work

  • Contract: you join Alan as an employee, ideally at 80% or more, and at least 60%. You can keep some clinical practice outside Alan.

  • Team: you are part of the Women's Health product team and of Alan's health professionals community.

  • Location: our headquarters are in Paris. You can be based abroad, as long as you speak French fluently and know the French healthcare system well.

  • Remote work: we offer remote work flexibility, but we value in-person collaboration.

🔄 What to expect from our recruitment process

  1. Application Review: we read your CV and application.

  2. Screening interview (45 to 60 minutes): your path, your motivation for this role, and practical points such as your availability.

  3. Technical interview: a short written case at home (60 to 90 minutes), including a situation where clinical and product needs conflict, then a live discussion of your answers.

  4. Alaner Fit interview: a conversation about how we work at Alan and whether it suits you.

  5. Alan Day: an on-site day where you prepare concrete use cases, present them to a panel and meet the people you would work with.

  6. Reference calls, including at least one with a non-medical colleague you have worked with.

Important note: we hire people, not roles.

If you're excited about this opportunity but don't check every box, we'd love to hear from you. Everyone, no matter how underrepresented, should feel free to apply, as it can only bring learnings or success.

If you identify yourself as a woman: did you know that research shows women often apply only when meeting 100% of requirements?

💡 You want to know more about Alan?

  • Perks & Benefits: Alaners are provided with a stimulating environment and perks ensuring they are happy, efficient and spend only high-quality time with co-workers.

  • A strong culture: People joining Alan are often surprised and delighted by our innovative working method. We have a set of cultural values that guide our approach to work.

  • Check out our About Alan and Career pages for more info.
